entry.title: Strategic Repayment and Latent Fragility in Financial Networks: Why Banks Withhold Payable Liquidity
entry.summary:
A network in which every bank pays in full can nevertheless admit a self-fulfilling settlement freeze under the same balance-sheet fundamentals. Thus, observing full repayment does not establish the uniqueness or robustness of the payment equilibrium. We derive this result from a precautionary-liquidity choice: banks may delay otherwise feasible payments to insure an interim funding need, trading a positive settlement-discipline cost against the marginal value of retained cash.

Source: arXiv Economics (econ.EM, econ.GN, econ.TH) · Tags: #econometrics #macroeconomics #quant-finance #decision-theory

entry.title: Paying Creators for Training Data Can Increase AI Displacement. Generative AI increasingly competes with creators while using their content as training data.
entry.summary:
Generative AI increasingly competes with creators while using their content as training data. In response, policymakers have called for platforms to compensate creators for training data use and allow opting out. We study how such policies affect creator displacement in a model of a platform where creators choose whether to contribute training data and consumers choose between purchasing from creators and prompting generative AI trained on their content.

Source: arXiv Economics (econ.EM, econ.GN, econ.TH) · Tags: #econometrics #macroeconomics #decision-theory #ml-theory

entry.title: Who Observes Whom: Network Rationalizability and Its Complexity
entry.summary:
Nash equilibrium and rationalizability sit at opposite informational extremes: the former presumes that each player knows all opponents' strategies, the latter that players reason from common knowledge of rationality alone. When visibility is partial and asymmetric, we study the solution concepts induced by a directed \emph{observation network} $G$ in which an edge $i\to j$ means that $i$ observes $j$'s strategy. A set of profiles is \emph{self-sustaining} if every profile in it can be justified, for every player, by conjectures from the same set that agree with everything the player observes.

Source: arXiv Economics (econ.EM, econ.GN, econ.TH) · Tags: #econometrics #macroeconomics #decision-theory #algorithms

entry.title: Leverage-Enhanced Sampling Owen Method for Explainable Artificial Intelligence
entry.summary:
Recently, the Shapley value has been widely applied in machine learning for feature importance analysis and model explainability. The multilinear extension of games proposed by Owen (1972) expresses the Shapley value as the integral of partial derivatives along the main diagonal of the cube. Direct evaluation of this integral requires exponential-time computation of the partial derivatives.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems #ml-theory

entry.title: A Polynomial-Time Algorithm for Constant-Factor EFX Allocations of Chores
entry.summary:
We study the fair division of indivisible chores among agents with additive disutilities, focusing on the central fairness notion of envy-freeness up to any chore (EFX), and its multiplicative approximations. Although the existence of constant-factor approximations to EFX are known, computing such an allocation in polynomial time remained open. We resolve this question by giving an algorithm that, for every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, computes a $(3+\varepsilon)$-EFX allocation in time polynomial in the input length and $1/\varepsilon$.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems #agents

entry.title: Why Cassini's Oval Could Not Replace Kepler's Ellipse?. In the later seventeenth century, Kepler's ellipse was not yet accepted.
entry.summary:
In the later seventeenth century, Kepler's ellipse was not yet accepted. Ward claimed that Boulliau's conic hypothesis amounted to a Ptolemaic equant at the ellipse's empty focus, and built his own model on it. Around 1675--1680, Giovanni Domenico Cassini proposed another curve, the ``oval'', a genus-1 quartic with no closed-form Kepler equation; yet its eccentric anomaly shares exactly the leading coefficient of Kepler's, and its empty focus is, for the Sun, 38 times closer to a true equant than the ellipse's.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems

entry.title: Nearly Settling the Complexity of Connected $\varepsilon$-Envy-Free Cake Cutting
entry.summary:
Envy-free cake cutting has been one of the central problems in fair division. In cake cutting, agents' preferences over the cake are accessed through Robertson--Webb (RW) queries. For three or more agents, no algorithm that makes finitely many RW queries can always find a contiguous, exactly envy-free allocation.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems #algorithms #agents

entry.title: Percolation under Edge-Reversal: Creation and Destruction of Strong Connectivity in Directed Networks
entry.summary:
We study how the connectivity of a directed network changes when each edge is independently reversed with probability $p$, while the underlying connections remain fixed. Reversal changes the in- and out-degrees, and we derive the exact transformation of the joint in--out-degree distribution and characterize its evolution under repeated reversal. However, the transformation does not rewire the network, and every edge still connects the same pair of vertices.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems

entry.title: Borrowed Strength, Imported Risk: Capability Gaps and Reception Govern Heterogeneous LLM Debate
entry.summary:
Heterogeneous LLM debate is often attributed to collective reasoning that creates capability beyond any member. In the matched panels we study, the aggregate gain is dominated by capability transfer: a peer supplies task competence and receivers absorb a measurable fraction. Across nine matched directions, honest benefit and first-exchange adversarial exposure open when the peer has a positive same-task advantage, and honest gain is closely described by the empirical decomposition $ΔA_d^{\mathrm{hon}}\approxκΓ_d^+ρ_d$, the product of that advantage and the receiver's reception.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems #agents

entry.title: A Combinatorial Characterization of Immunity to the Strong Braess Paradox
entry.summary:
In a nonatomic congestion game, a strong Braess paradox occurs when reducing resource costs, population demands, or both increases at least one population's equilibrium cost. We characterize immunity when each population's available strategies form a fixed finite family of nonempty subsets of a common resource set. Immunity means that no such paradox can arise for any nonnegative continuous nondecreasing resource cost functions common to all populations and any positive demand vector.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems

entry.title: Same Papers, Different Verdicts: Tracing Version Drift in LLM Peer Review. Venues and benchmarks read LLM review scores as measurements of a paper, while providers replace their models within months.
entry.summary:
Venues and benchmarks read LLM review scores as measurements of a paper, while providers replace their models within months. We audit twenty frontier models from OpenAI, Google and Anthropic on ICLR 2027 submissions while they were under review, with tests registered before the decisions. Between an earlier and a later version of Claude Opus and of Gemini, the share of papers placed on the accept side falls by 52 and 53 percentage points on 183 and 60 randomly drawn submissions, and by 43 to 79 points in six further paired comparisons, with no paper moving up in any of them.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems #llm #ml-theory
